verdict.rationale: n8n's source is publicly readable on GitHub and docs describe it as "fair-code licensed" (n8n-docs-12, n8n-docs-29), but this is a Sustainable Use License, not an OSI-approved open-source license, and community commentary explicitly flags this: "Not really OSS" (n8n-comm-19). So while code is viewable, the claim of an 'open license' is contradicted by license terms and community consensus. Missing for 10: an actual OSI-approved open-source license, and vendor acknowledgment that fair-code restricts commercial/competing use.
